messages:
sara: Heads up — hit a weird capacity hit this morning in us-west-2. Scheduler reports a high fragmentation ratio (0.42) and a bunch of small idle slots that the bin-packer won't use. Impacting low-latency customer routes.

josh: Ugh, saw increased evictions too? Any correlation with the weekend image-gen spike hypothesis? :thinking:

sara: Evictions up ~18% last 24h. Forecasting shows a 2.3–2.7x GPU-hour bump next weekend from marketing campaign + holidays. Fragmentation seems to be the main limiter, not raw GPU count.

mike: Can you paste the frag metric query? I want to see distribution across instance types.

sara: frag_ratio = idle_gpus_in_slots_small / total_idle_gpus over 1h windows. Quick probe: `fleetctl probe --region us-west-2 --metric frag_ratio --window 3600` returned 0.42 avg and spikes to 0.6 on 2 smaller AZs.

anne: Two ideas: 1) temporary reduce strictness of affinity so larger jobs can spread into those small slots (loosen packing constraint), 2) introduce eviction_smoothing to avoid thrash when we quickly change priorities.

josh: +1 on smoothing. Current policy uses instantaneous score, so a minor TTL bump causes immediate preemptions. We should apply a moving average over X secs. Proposed config: 
```
scheduler:
  binpack:
    fragmentation_threshold: 0.2
    eviction_smoothing_window_sec: 600
    preemptible_fill_ratio: 0.85
```
Seems safe to start at 600s.

mike: What about fairness? If we allow packing across tenants we might starve low-priority bursty jobs. Need imitation of soft-share: allow pack but track tenant fill and enforce max_fill_percent per tenant per node.

sara: Agreed, propose canary rollout on 10% of capacity in us-west-2 with tenant caps and telemetry dashboards. Also add alert if tenant_fill > 0.7 for 5m.

josh: Can we simulate quickly? I can run the binpack sim with the new smoothing and cap heuristics. Command I use: `tools/binpack-sim --input recent-workload.json --smoothing 600 --tenant-cap 0.7`

anne: Add cost check: looser packing might reduce fragmentation but increase avg tail latency for preemptible tasks, affecting SLO. We need to tie the sim results to token-hour cost delta and p99 latency.

mike: If sim looks good, I'll prep a rollout PR and include a feature flag `eviction_smoothing_v2` that we can flip. Also plan a rollback: revert flag -> immediate revert of smoothing weights.

sara: I'll schedule the canary for Friday 03:00 UTC to catch weekend traffic pattern, notify SRE and oncall. Also posting the quick runbook in #eng-oncall.

gpu-bot: deploy-bot: Canary job queued for group: runtime-canary-10pct, estimated 45m job. Logs at https://deploys.internal/reports/1751236789

josh: I'll kick off the sim now and share results in this thread. Expect initial numbers in ~20m.

sara: Thanks all — priority is reducing avoidable evictions before the weekend. Will follow-up with sim output and rollout checklist. :eyes:
